label: QA-01
title: abi.encodePacked() with dynamic-type arguments passed to keccak256 — used only for revert message formatting, no hash collision attack surface
borderlineNote: Originally flagged as potential-medium pending usage context. Code review confirms: the abi.encodePacked call at AYieldStrategy.sol line 340 is used exclusively to concatenate a human-readable revert message string (literal text + timestamp integer converted to string). No hash result is stored, compared, or used for access control or entity identity. The dynamic argument (the _uint256ToString output) is a display-only string. There is no hash collision attack surface.
description: The keccak256(abi.encodePacked(...)) at line 340 constructs a revert message string embedding a formatted timestamp for human readability, not a hash used for access control, entity identification, or state gating. The standard Slither/Aderyn warning does not apply here; this is a false-positive at Medium.
impact: None. The keccak256/abi.encodePacked is used only for revert message construction. Two different timestamps producing the same concatenated string would only affect the human-readable error message, not any state or access control.
attackPath: No attack path exists: the encodePacked output is passed directly into revert() as an error string
